questions.question: Matchstick squares in a row use 4, 7, 10 and 13 matches. Describe the pattern and find shape 10.
questions.expected_answer: Each new square adds 3 matches because it shares one side with the square before it. A rule is shape number times 3, plus 1. Shape 10 uses 10 times 3 plus 1, which is 31 matches.

questions.question: Dot triangles have 1, 3, 6 and 10 dots. Find the next two and explain.
questions.expected_answer: The differences are 2, 3 and 4, growing by 1 each time, so the next differences are 5 and 6. 10 plus 5 is 15, and 15 plus 6 is 21.

questions.question: Explain why shape 20 of the matchstick pattern is not double shape 10.
questions.expected_answer: Shape 10 has 31 matches: 30 for the ten squares plus 1 for the first side. Doubling gives 62, which counts the first side twice. Shape 20 is 20 times 3 plus 1, which is 61.
